learning_objective: 🎯 Explore the different avatars a business can take—from a one-man army (Sole Proprietorship) to a giant corporate empire (Joint Stock Company)!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: A business owned, managed, and controlled by a single individual. It's easy to form, but the owner has 'unlimited liability' (personal assets can be sold to pay business debts).

A unique form of business found only in India, owned and carried out by the members of an undivided Hindu family. The eldest member is called the 'Karta', who has unlimited liability, while other members (coparceners) have limited liability.
When two or more people agree to run a business and share its profits and losses. They sign an agreement called a 'Partnership Deed'.

An artificial person created by law, having a separate legal entity, perpetual succession (it doesn't die if owners change), and a common seal. The liability of members (shareholders) is strictly limited to their shares.

fun_activity.title: 🏢 The Business Matchmaker
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine you want to start a local tea stall. What form is best? (Sole Proprietorship!). Now imagine you want to build a ₹500 crore smartphone manufacturing plant. What form? (Joint Stock Company!). Match the business size and risk to the right organization!

exam_tips: 📌 'Unlimited Liability' is a major disadvantage of Sole Proprietorship and Partnership. Ensure you clearly define it in exams.
📌 Distinguish clearly between a Public Company (minimum 7 members, no maximum limit) and a Private Company (minimum 2, maximum 200 members).
📌 Cooperative societies work on the principle of 'One man, one vote', regardless of the amount of capital contributed by a member.
quick_recap: ⭐ Registration of a Partnership is optional, but registration of a Joint Stock Company is legally compulsory.
⭐ A company is distinct from its members; shareholders own the company, but the Board of Directors manages it.
⭐ Minor as a partner: A minor can only be admitted to the 'benefits' of an existing partnership with the consent of all partners.
